messages:
Marta: FYI, acme-corp tenant provisioning failing with SCIM 403 right after we pushed the new RBAC restrictions on service principals. customer reported user create failing.
Ben: can you paste the SCIM response and any proxy logs? 403 could be upstream (IdP) or our side.
Marta: pasted snippets below; proxy log shows a KMS decrypt denial immediately before the 403 which looks suspicious.
Marta: ```[2026-06-02T09:11:07Z] scim-proxy ERROR req=rdw-21 decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/scim-proxy-role/session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/0a1b2c3d-4e5f-6a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
 at com.redwood.scim.internal.KmsClient.decrypt(KmsClient.java:122)
```
Anya: that error pattern usually means the CMK key policy doesn't include the role or there's a condition on the key policy that our role doesn't satisfy (source account, principal tags, source IP). Did the infra team touch key policies or rotate aliases recently?
Marta: infra confirmed they tightened cross-account grants as part of the RBAC hardening last week and rotated some aliases. we likely relied on the previous allow.
Sam: quick checklist to triage: 1) confirm which principal ARN is making the decrypt (assume role ARN in the log), 2) check CMK key policy for explicit Principal/SID for scim-proxy-role, 3) check for conditional statements (aws:SourceAccount, aws:PrincipalTag), 4) verify alias points to same key id which has grants.
Ben: run an aws kms decrypt locally as the assumed role to repro (or simulate via sts assume-role + AWS CLI). Decrypt failing locally means it's definitely KMS policy/role issue, not Okta.
Marta: I repro'd with the scim-proxy role creds:
Marta: ```$ aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://attrs.enc --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/0a1b2c3d-4e5f-6a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
An error occurred (AccessDeniedException) when calling the Decrypt operation: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/scim-proxy-role/session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt
```
Anya: OK. Two remediation paths: update the CMK key policy to add the scim-proxy-role explicitly (recommended to include a condition aws:SourceAccount to reduce blast radius), or alter the IAM role to include a kms:Decrypt permission with the key ARN as resource (but note KMS evaluates key policy first). Long-term: document CMK dependencies in RBAC change runbooks.
Marta: opened PR to add the role to the key policy and included a note about aws:SourceAccount condition. PR: https://git.redwood.com/r/redwood/infra/+/PR-1027 (diff includes new statement for scim-proxy-role and a short justification).
idp-bot: okta scim log tenant=acme-corp call_id=xyz-20260602-1 status=403 time=2026-06-02T09:11:08Z reason=forbidden
Ben: after policy fix make sure to validate CloudTrail entries for KMS Decrypt with correlation id so we can prove the decrypt succeeded and match it to the Okta 403. Also check for any KMS Grant objects that might be stale.
Marta: updated policy applied. re-ran the create flow with X-Correlation-ID header included. HTTP 201 returned.
Marta: ```# post-fix test
$ curl -i -X POST https://scim.redwood.com/Users -H \"X-Correlation-ID: rdw-21\" -d '{\"userName\":\"jane.smith\"}'
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
```
Sam: follow-ups / lessons learned: - add a small e2e regression test in infra pipeline that exercises SCIM flows against a test CMK on every RBAC/key-policy change - add an alert when CloudTrail shows KMS:Decrypt AccessDenied for the scim-proxy-role more than once in an hour - add a step in the RBAC rollout template to enumerate dependent CMKs (owner + key-id) and notify key owners before changes.
Anya: also update our incident runbook: section 'RBAC/key rotations' should include commands to lookup KMS events in CloudTrail and how to query key policy quickly. Example: `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=Decrypt --max-results 50` and `aws kms get-key-policy --key-id <key-id> --policy-name default`.
Marta: filing a process gap ticket for privileged key rotation without dependent-grants update: SEC-4284. tagging infra as reviewer.
Ben: small docs action: add a checkbox to the RBAC rollout PR template: "Confirm dependent CMKs and update key policies/grants".
Marta: I'll add that to the rollout checklist and link SEC-4284. marking customer impact resolved.
Sam: thanks all. :thumbsup:
